These Appeals, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

These appeals are filed by the petitioners seeking enhancement of compensation challenging the common judgment dated 04.02.2013 passed in M.V.C.Nos.171, 172 and 173/2012 by the learned Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court and M.A.C.T., Channarayapatna ('the Tribunal' in short).
NC: 2023:KHC:20966 2.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 14.05.2010, one Kumari Lalitha, who was admitted to hospital at Hassan, was being carried to the hospital at Bangalore for higher treatment by one Suchitra, Rekha and Bettegowda in an ambulance bearing No.KA-13/A- 6511; at about 3.15 a.m.,
near Kattarighatta gate, due to patient Lalitha was getting vomiting sensation, the ambulance was stopped by the side of the road.
At that time, a KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-13/F-430 came from behind and dashed against the rear side of the ambulance killing the patient Kumari Lalitha and Suchitra at spot and injuring Rekha.

Seeking compensation, the dependants of Kumari Lalitha and Suchitra and the injured Rekha have approached the Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Ramachandra vs The Divisional Controller on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101452472/
3 Act, 1988.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Ramachandra vs The Divisional Controller on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim was opposed by the KSRTC and after taking the evidence, the Tribunal passed the NC: 2023:KHC:20966 impugned judgment awarding compensation.
Pleading inadequacy, the petitioners have filed these appeals on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.M.T.Madhu on behalf of Sri.Girish B.Baladare, learned Counsel for the petitioners, Smt.Sumangala A.Swamy, learned counsel for KSRTC, Sri.Lakshminarasappa,
learned counsel for National Insurance Company and Sri.Sunil Kumar on behalf of Sri.H.S.Lingaraj,
learned Counsel for the Oriental Insurance Company.

5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident is of the year 2010;
deceased Kumari Lalitha was 23 years old unmarried, working as Staff Nurse and drawing salary of Rs.10,000/- per month, the Tribunal has not considered future prospects while assessing the compensation.
Deceased Suchitra was aged 30 years, was doing household and animal husbandry earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but it is not considered by the Tribunal, so also future prospects.

The injured Rekha NC: 2023:KHC:20966 has suffered fracture of both bones of right forearm and suffered fracture of vertebra and she has suffered disability of 55% and by doing household work and animal husbandry, she was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but it has not been considered by the Tribunal and sought for enhancement of compensation.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the KSRTC has contended that without arranging any signal, the Ambulance was parked on the road and for this reason, the KSRTC bus was forced to hit against the hind portion of the Ambulance.

Complete negligence is on the driver of Ambulance and contended that attribution of 50% of contributory negligence on the driver of bus is not proper and sought for its reduction and it has to be fastened against the Ambulance, further supported the impugned judgment insofar as assessment of compensation.

7. Learned counsel for Insurance Company has contended that at the time of accident, driver of the NC: 2023:KHC:20966 ambulance did not carry valid driving licence and for this reason, there is violation of policy terms and conditions and the Tribunal has rightly fastened liability against the owner and the Insurance Company and to this extent, he has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Nanjappan and Others1.
8.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Nanjappan and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties and also perused the materials on record.
9. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, death of Kumari Lalitha and Suchitra and injuries sustained by another inmate of ambulance Smt.Rekha.

KSRTC bus came behind and hit against the stationed Ambulance on the road, the Tribunal has held that both the drivers of ambulance as well as KSRTC bus are equally held responsible directing the KSRTC to pay 50% of AIR 2004 SC 1630 NC: 2023:KHC:20966 compensation and the owner of the ambulance to pay remaining 50% of compensation.
10. Since there is no appeal filed by the respondents questioning the finding recorded by the Tribunal, question of determining the percentage of contributory negligence does not arise.

The only Ramachandra vs The Divisional Controller on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101452472/
4 issue is regarding liability fastened against the owner of the ambulance.

entities.text: Ramachandra vs The Divisional Controller on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As found from the material on record, the accident took place on 14.05.2010 and on that day, the driver of ambulance was holding only Learners' Licence and he obtained regular licence subsequently i.e., on 21.05.2010.
Hence, it is a clear case of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Ambulance is a special vehicle where patients are being carried in cases of emergency and it requires a driver with specialized skill.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment referred supra laid down that in case of violation of terms of the policy conditions, the insurer is liable to pay compensation at the first instance and to recover it from the insured.

In view of the same, the Tribunal has NC:
2023:KHC:20966 lost sight of the said principle and directed the owner of the Ambulance to pay compensation to the extent of 50%, which is incorrect and in view of the principle of 'pay and recovery', the Insurance Company of the Ambulance has to pay compensation and to recover the same from the owner of the Ambulance.
11. Adverting to the assessment of compensation is concerned, the deceased Lalitha was working as Staff Nurse, she was aged 23 years, unmarried and the petitioners are her parents.
Her pay slip points out that she was drawing salary of Rs.7,433/- per month and her job is permanent one.
12. Insofar as deceased Suchitra is concerned, she was a housewife and aged 30 years and she is married.
She has a dependant husband, a child and in-laws.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.4,500/- whereas in the year 2010, the notional income of a person with no proof of income is assessed at Rs.5,500/-.

The - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:20966 Tribunal has lost sight of the principles laid down in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others2 regarding assessment of quantum of compensation in case of this nature.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The age of the deceased Suchitra was 30 years and if the principles of Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another3 is applied, the multiplier applicable to deceased Lalitha is '18' and that of Suchitra is '17'.

entities.text: Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Deceased Kumari Lalitha was permanently employed, hence, future prospects has to be taken at 50% and for that of the deceased Suchitra at 40%.

Lalitha was having dependant parents whereas Suchitra was having four dependants, but her in-laws cannot be taken into consideration as dependants, only her husband and minor child can be considered as dependants for the purpose of assessing compensation under conventional heads.

13. Insofar as assessment of compensation for the death of Lalitha is concerned, her income at Rs.7,433/- (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20966 and addition of 50% future prospects comes to Rs.3,716/- = Rs.11,149/-; if 50% is excluded towards personal expenses, then it comes to Rs.5,574/- x 12 x 18 multiplier =
Rs.12,03,984/- towards loss of dependency.

Under conventional heads, towards loss of love and affection, Rs.15,000/- each to the parents, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.10,000/-

5 towards funeral expenses is added, the total compensation comes to Rs.12,53,984/- as against Rs.6,29,852/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby an enhancement of Rs.6,24,132/-.

sentences.text:
14. Insofar as death of Suchitra is concerned, her income could be taken at Rs.5,500/- + Rs.2,200/-
(40% of future prospects) comes to Rs.7,700/-.

If 1/3rd is deducted, net income comes to Rs.5,134/-
x 12 x multiplied by 17 = Rs.10,47,336/-.
Towards loss of love and affection to the husband and minor child, a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is assessed and Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses.
Then the total compensation comes to Rs.10,97,336/- as - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:20966 against Rs.6,62,000/-, thereby an enhancement of Rs.4,35,336/-.

15. Insofar as injuries to Smt.Rekha is concerned, the medical records including the evidence of PW- 2/Dr.H.S.Ravi point out that she has suffered fracture of both bones of right forearm, fracture of right acetabulum, diastatis with pubic rami fracture.
The opinion of the treated doctor points out that she has suffered 25% of disability to right upper limb and 30% of disability to right lower limb.
The cross-examination of the treated doctor did not point out anything that he has made wrong assessment.
The injured is a lady; she has suffered fracture of both bones of right forearm and also suffered fracture of pubic bone.
For a lady aged 30 years, doing agriculture, the said disability would certainly affect her earning capacity.
The Tribunal has assessed 1/3rd of the total limb disability as whole body disability at 18%.
I do not find any irregularity committed by the Tribunal in assessing so.

Having taken into consideration the date of - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:20966 accident, the petitioner having sustained such injuries, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation towards pain and suffering at Rs.40,000/- and Rs.80,000/- towards medical expenses.

The nature of injury will certainly affect her to be fit to resume her work and therefore, loss of income during laid up of four months is taken, it comes to Rs.22,000/- @
Rs.5,500/- per month.
The petitioner was under hospitalization for one month and thereby attendant charge of Rs.5,500/- is assessed.
A sum of Rs.2,000/- towards traveling expenses and loss of amenities and discomfort shall be assessed at Rs.40,000/-.
The loss of income due to disability will be: Rs.5,500/- per month x 12 x 17 multiplier x 18% comes to Rs.2,01,960/-.

Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to just compensation of Rs.3,91,460/- as against Rs.1,53,500/-
awarded by the Tribunal, thereby an enhancement of Rs.2,37,960/-.
16. As regards apportionment is concerned, the Tribunal has rightly recorded that both drivers are equally liable for the accident.
Thereby these appeals filed by the petitioners for enhancement of compensation as well as fastening of liability against the owner of the Ambulance are deserved to be allowed in part.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) All three appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment is modified.

(iii) The petitioners in M.F.A.No.5746/2013 are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.6,24,132/-, the petitioners in M.F.A.No.5745/2013 are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,35,336/-
and the petitioner in M.F.A.No.5747/2013 is entitled for enhanced compensation of - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:20966 Rs.2,37,960/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization.

(iv) The respondent No.3/Insurance Company is directed to deposit 50% of the enhanced compensation within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and to recover the same from the owner of the Ambulance/respondent No.2 in the same proceedings.
(v) The respondent No.1/KSRTC is directed to deposit remaining 50% of the enhanced compensation within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(vi) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records.
